deviations: BRAIN PROMPT ACCESS (accepted practice, user-ruled 2026-08-22, pending F128 codification): this harness exposes no tool-less subagent type. The extraction brain ran on model opus with the whole prompt inlined and a binding instruction to use NO tools, and it used none (0 tool calls). The judge (3 samples), thesis, implication and narrator brains ran on model opus with Read on their own pre-split prompt files and one Write to their own answer file - their prompts run 134-284 KB and inlining them would not fit. The user accepted this as standard practice on 2026-08-22; recorded here for the run record, not as an open question.

GATHERER TOOL-WALL: NOW STRUCTURAL (the 2026-08-22 ruling applied for the first time in a cycle). The three reader-gatherers, the series reader and the three chart researchers were all dispatched as the registered `web-gatherer` subagent type, whose tool set is exactly Read/Write/WebSearch/WebFetch and which structurally excludes Bash. The F88 injection wall is a real wall again, not a prompt-level instruction as it was on 2026-08-21.

READ-TOOL PAGINATION (prompt splitting - accepted practice, user-ruled 2026-08-22): the CLI emits each brain prompt as a single-line JSON field, and the judge `user` field (134 KB on one line) exceeds the Read tool's per-call token cap, which paginates by LINE. Judge sample 1 failed outright on this; sample 2 worked around it with Grep. For every later seam the coordinator pre-split each emitted prompt into `<seam>-system.txt`, `<seam>-schema.json` and numbered `<seam>-user-partN.txt` chunks, and the brain read the chunks in order. Sample 1 was re-dispatched on the chunked files and succeeded. No prompt text was altered - only how it is stored on disk for the subagent to read.

BLOB PROVENANCE CORRECTION (AFK-default): gatherer g3's Marvell/Google blob claimed the SEC 8-K URL (sec.gov) but EDGAR returned 403 to that gatherer, and the text actually came from search-surfaced 8-K excerpts plus a 24/7 Wall St. page it did fetch. The coordinator rewrote ONLY that blob's `url` and `source` to the page actually fetched, so `ingest` stamps it `secondary` instead of `primary`; the SEC URL is retained in the blob's `chase.primaryFound`. The correction can only lower claimed trust, never inflate it. Blob `content` was not read or altered.

ACRONYM ALLOWLIST EDIT (AFK-default): the daily report render refused to ship with `unknown all-caps token(s) above the appendix divider: MLCC`. The token comes from an already-gated finding (the DIGITIMES MLCC lead-time story), so rewriting it would have meant re-running extraction over findings already written to the store. `MLCC` was added to registry/acronyms.json (allowed) instead - the fix the gate's own error message prescribes, and the same route a prior cycle used for `CS-4`. registry/acronyms.json is voice-lint DATA and is not embedded in any emitted brain prompt, so no F6 prompt hash moved; the full suite was re-run to confirm.
